Scaling the ledger to a billion entries

Our ledger crossed a billion entries last spring. The write path was never the problem: appending double-entry rows is cheap. The problem was the daily reconciliation job, which read every entry written that day and compared it against the settlement file from our bank.

We moved reconciliation from a nightly batch to a streaming job keyed by settlement date, partitioned the ledger by seller, and kept both entries of a transfer inside the same partition so a transfer is always balanced within one shard. Reconciliation went from four hours to eleven minutes.

The lesson we keep relearning: in a ledger, the interesting scaling limit is almost never the write throughput. It is whatever has to read everything back and prove the numbers agree.
